explanation: The cords, called khipu or quipu, stored numbers in knots using a base-10 place system. Some scholars think they also recorded words, such as names and stories.

claims.text: Inca officials recorded numerical information, such as census and tribute data, on knotted cords called khipu.
The Inca did not keep their records on notched sticks, painted pebbles or clay tokens.
Khipu recorded numbers with knots in a base-10 positional system.
Some scholars argue that khipu also recorded non-numerical information such as names or narratives.
